notes: Company: SummitRidge Conversant Systems — mid-market SaaS providing embeddable chat agents for e-commerce and mid-sized telco support teams.
Primary ask: evaluate Hosted API for chat/agent flows, streaming required. Goal: <1.5s first-token for typical 1-2 turn exchanges (avg prompt size ~120 tokens).

Context: product team building agent product with tool-calling (ticket creation, customer DB lookup, order status). Tool calls must be low-latency; prefer function/tool calling over model-side parsing.

Proof-of-concept plan: 2-week POC on Hosted API -> run synthetic + real traffic replay to measure first-token latency and streaming behaviour; if good, discuss Dedicated pricing and committed capacity for predictable burst handling.

Traffic profile: peak concurrency ~120 concurrent agents, expected steady 40-60 qps, heavy diurnal spikes (EAST coast retail hours). Cost sensitivity moderate — will trade slightly higher cost for guaranteed latency under SLOs.

Security: SOC2 required by procurement; already use SSO (SAML) and expect KMS integration for keys. Need audit logs and retention controls (30-90d). No hard residency requirement but will ask for audit trails and tenant isolation for Dedicated.

POC notes: initial token throughput tested on day 3 — median first-token 0.9s, 95th perc 1.9s during synthetic bursts (need to get 95th <1.5s). Streaming works end-to-end but chunking behavior differs vs competitor A; SE suggested adjustments to chunk size and keepalive settings.

Integration: wants tool-calling pattern: pre-flight lookup -> call external ticketing API -> stream final message incl ticket id. Need examples and SDK code snippets. SE to provide Node + Python helper for streaming + tool-call orchestration.

Quote from demo (3/02): 'If we can't guarantee the first token under 1.5s for most cases, ops will flag as risky for enterprise customers.' — Head of Product. Emphasis on 99th percentile avoidance for critical flows.

Commercial: initial ARR target $75-200k; considering Dedicated if we can get committed throughput discount and SLA-backed latency. Procurement expects contract language around uptime and fallback model behavior.

Operational asks: ability to pin model versions for rollouts, canary routing to cheaper variants, transparent token-level cost dashboard. Redwood Console demo was well received — they want route-level latency histograms.
